quotes.text: MCQAConverter processes 8.9K questions from 8 MCQA benchmarks (MedQA, MedMCQA, 6 MMLU subsets)

rationale: Source datasets are named (MedQA, MedMCQA, MMLU subsets, MIMIC-III/IV, PubMed/PMC passages) and Table 5 gives sample counts. No dataset version or snapshot date and no explicit route from a task back to its source record appear in S1-S3, so this is partial.

quotes.text: All patient data is **synthetic**. No real patient information is used.

rationale: Origin (converted public benchmarks, knowledge mining, seed tasks) and a synthetic-patient statement are given, plus an Apache-2.0 repo licence. The licences or terms of the source datasets are not documented, so the level-2 requirement is unmet. Note the paper also says EHR episodes are extracted from MIMIC-III/IV, which sits uneasily with the README claim that all patient data is synthetic.

quotes.text: sampled without replacement from the same domain distribution as training

rationale: The validation split is described with a stated sampling design and per-domain task counts. No comparison of patient features against any named target population is reported, so this is the weakest partial credit.

quotes.text: Rule-based SafetyViolation detection with 50+ violation patterns across 5 severity levels

rationale: A rule-based unsafe-output detector with a 5-level taxonomy (Appendix H) is part of the reward, so an unsafe-output check exists. No bias test is reported in S1-S3 and no safety-specific results are tabulated. Code-only adversarial safety tests (S4 safety_eval) do not count as reporting.

quotes.text: zero data contamination verified via test-set fingerprinting
TT-OPD validation accuracy is computed on a held-out set of 307 tasks

rationale: A held-out validation set is the developer-side control and test-set fingerprinting is the stated overlap check; the README repeats the claim. The fingerprinting result is asserted rather than shown with figures, but it is a measured check.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. No statement that the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time, and no mechanism named. The hint-masking described for the teacher concerns training-time outcome hints, not run-time gold isolation.

quotes.text: All servers call **live public APIs** — no local data bundled, internet required
local weights, a local sglang server, a local FTS5 index

rationale: The core path uses a local FTS5 index of 828,473 passages, local weights and a local sglang server, so data is pinned. The released Docker MCP environment for trajectory synthesis and evaluation depends on live public APIs, and the cluster README says the environment is not reproducible from the frozen requirements alone. That leaves a live service, so level 1.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No scripted reference solution run through the grader and no solvability evidence is reported. Synthetic trajectory generators in S4 are not reported oracle runs.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. WRITE tools exist (orders, prescriptions, notes) and expected actions include record_diagnosis, so the item applies and NA is not warranted. Grading is by answer match, expected-tool coverage and rule-based safety penalties, with no check of unchanged or out-of-scope state.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, no per-metric chance rate and no design argument that trivial behaviour fails. The paper notes format-reward dilution but does not report how easily coverage-based process scores could be gamed.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. No do-nothing or random agent result is reported. Base text and Base+AR are untrained model baselines, not trivial agents.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. Graders (exact match, ROUGE/BLEU, BiomedBERT, expected-action coverage, rule-based safety) are described but no validation of them, with figures or reference-solution tests, is reported.

quotes.text: seed: 42
"temperature": 0.0,

rationale: Seeds and temperature settings appear only in code and configs (seed 42 in a training config, temperature 0.0 in the log-probability evaluator). S1-S3 state no seed, decoding policy or repeated-run policy, so this is the code-only level.

quotes.text: mean accuracy of 59.5% ( \pm 1.4 pp) over steps 40–60

rationale: A spread (±1.4 pp over training steps 40-60) is given for TT-OPD validation accuracy. No CI or significance test accompanies the headline comparisons in Table 1 (+3.9 pp average, best on 10 of 18 benchmarks).

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4. No number of evaluation runs per task behind Table 1, no evaluation seed or decoding controls and no independence statement appear in S1-S3. Generations per prompt (3) is a training rollout setting, not an evaluation run count.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4. Table 1 and the README table carry no CI or SE, no resampling unit and no treatment of clustering of tasks within patients or templates. The only spread is a training-step variation figure.
searched: S1, S2, S3, S4. No identical-rerun information, no action- or state-level agreement and no pass^k metric are reported.

quotes.text: Qwen3.5-9B ( Qwen Team, 2025 )

rationale: The backbone is identified as Qwen3.5-9B with a Hugging Face reference and year, which is accepted for (i) but is a weak identifier. No evaluation decoding parameters are given in S1-S3. Only a dependency version (veRL v0.8.0+) is stated, with no harness tag or commit matching the reported numbers.

quotes.text: Tools are registered via the @is_tool(ToolType) decorator, which supports four types: READ (queries), WRITE (state modifications), THINK (internal reasoning), and GENERIC (submit).
Invalid JSON or unknown tool names return error messages rather than crashing the episode.

rationale: OpenAI-compatible schemas are generated from every decorated tool, tools carry READ/WRITE/THINK/GENERIC types, and return and error behaviour is described. The READ/WRITE type is not part of the schema the agent receives (name, description, parameters only), though some descriptions imply writes, so the read-versus-write property does not reliably reach S5.

quotes.text: Order a new lab test for a patient. The test will be simulated
Analyze a medical image and return findings. In simulation mode,

contradiction_quotes.text: Base+AR uses the same multi-turn AgentRunner with 135 tools and 828K-passage KB as RL models
which means the paper's own Base+AR VQA row may itself be a toolless

rationale: S1-S3 report no tool conformance tests (the README lists only a unit-tests directory) and no explicit disclosure of simulated tool behaviour. Some agent-visible tool descriptions say outputs are simulated, so the disclosure reaches S5. A code comment says the original multimodal path never forwarded the tool catalog, which suggests the reported Base+AR VQA rows were toolless, against the paper's statement; flagged as a candidate contradiction only.

quotes.text: Clinical actions : ordering tests, prescribing medications, recording diagnoses.
Critical violations (severity 5: contraindication ignored, dangerous dosing, missed emergency) cap total reward at 0.1

rationale: Write tools are identified (WRITE type, W counts per domain, ordering, prescribing and note-writing) and unsafe prescribing is penalised via the severity taxonomy. S1-S3 do not state whether writes are executed, simulated or sandboxed. S5 tool descriptions such as the lab-order tool say the test will be simulated, so the S5 reach is true.

quotes.text: 60% coverage (proportion of expected tools called with matching arguments)

rationale: Grader inputs are named: answer string (exact match, ROUGE/BLEU, BiomedBERT), tool-call log coverage, rubric assertions and rule-based safety checks. No rationale is given for grading actions or transcripts instead of end state, and no validation on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates is reported.

quotes.text: TT-OPD validation accuracy is computed on a held-out set of 307 tasks

rationale: A held-out validation split is reported, but task files with correct answers and split lists are public in the repo, so this is partial. No controls on leakage through tools or retrieval and no canary or provenance marker appear in S1-S3; the fingerprinting claim concerns data overlap, not agent-channel leakage.

quotes.text: Category | Benchmark | Base (text) | Base+AR | GRPO | TT-OPD
Text QA | MedQA (USMLE) ( Jin et al., 2021 ) | 1,273 | Accuracy

rationale: Results are given per benchmark within four task categories, and Table 5 reports n per benchmark. No results by patient subgroup are reported although tasks carry age and sex fields. Per-domain results across the 10 clinical domains are not reported either.

quotes.text: All patient data is **synthetic**. No real patient information is used.
EHRConverter extracts MIMIC-III/IV admission episodes

rationale: The record source is stated (synthetic seed patients, converted benchmarks, MIMIC episodes), so (i) is present, though the README claim conflicts with the paper's use of MIMIC-derived episodes. No IRB, DUA or de-identification statement appears for real data. Data terms are not stated separately from the Apache-2.0 repo licence.
